text:
maria: Heads-up — canary for vega-2-int8 showed spike in funcall parse failures on the structured-output endpoint. Baseline was ~1.8%, canary bumped to ~3.9% across sampled traffic. Samples below.

sanjay: Ugh. Do you have sample outputs? Is it truncated JSON, or extra garbage?

maria: Mostly suffix garble and occasional missing closing brackets. Example snippet from canary logs (raw streaming capture):

```
{"action": "search", "args": {"q": "puppies"}}
...}#}
{"action": "open", "args": {"id": 123
```

maria: That was pulled from ~10k traces, 197 parse failures flagged by the strict schema checker.

oliver: Sounds like KV-cache chunk boundaries changed tokenization at int8. We saw token boundary drift when quantizing in previous PTQ runs. Quick tests: disable prefix caching for funcall routes and re-run canary.

anya: Also try a salvage path: run NDJSON salvage + json5-like tolerant parser as a postprocess before we mark it failed. In raven-lite experiments that recovered ~35–45% of failures without changing model outputs.

ci-bot: canary-run: vega-2-int8 | status: failed | parse-fail-rate: 3.9% | samples: 197 | commit: ab12cde | run_id: canary-2026-06-02-17

sanjay: If salvage brings it under 2% we can consider ship-with-parser-fallback. If not, fallback policy to serve fp16 for toolcall endpoints only while we debug.

maria: Plan of action: (1) disable prefix/KV cache for funcall routes in canary and re-run, (2) enable NDJSON salvage parser in postprocess for the canary cohort, (3) capture streaming-chunk token boundaries & sequence-lengths for failed traces, (4) gated A/B rollback to vega-2-fp16 for funcalls if parse-fail-rate >= 2.5%. I'll kick off the runs now.

oliver: Also instrument per-token logits delta for boundary tokens so we can see whether quant shifts cause punctuation token swaps.

anya: I'll add a small replay harness to feed failing prompts into fp16 vs int8 and unit-test the parser heuristics. Could automate salvage-heuristic weighting.

maria: Thanks — will post run summaries here. @ci-bot please attach the next run summary once complete. :thumbsup:
